lessons.title: The Spinning Hands of Nairobi's Clock Tower: What Is Really Happening?

quiz.prompt: At 12:00 the minute hand of a clock points straight up, towards the numeral 12. Which is the best prediction for where the tip of the hand will point at 12:15?
choices: Towards the numeral 9, on the left
Towards the numeral 3, on the right
Straight up, towards the numeral 12
Towards the numeral 6, at the bottom
quiz.rationale: A quarter of an hour later the minute hand has made a quarter turn clockwise, so it points to the 3. Learners who choose other positions are guessing the direction or the amount of turning.
quiz.placement: Predict: sketching three predicted positions of the hand on the blank clock-face worksheet

quiz.prompt: Four photographs show the minute hand of the University of Nairobi clock at 12:00, 12:15, 12:30 and 12:45. Which statement correctly describes what changed and what stayed the same?
choices: The hand turned into a mirror image of itself each time, and the centre moved
The hand slid sideways across the clock face, and its direction stayed the same
The length of the hand changed, and the direction it points stayed the same
The direction the hand points changed, and the length of the hand stayed the same
quiz.rationale: The learners' I Notice lists record that the hand points in a different direction each time, while its length and its centre point stay the same. The hand does not stretch, flip or slide.
quiz.placement: Observe: I Notice / I Wonder table and the class list of 'What stays the same' and 'What changed'

quiz.prompt: Which of these is the best 'I Wonder' question to post on the Driving Question Board after watching the clock images?
choices: The clock is on the Administration Block.
The minute hand moves.
How much has the hand turned between 12:00 and 12:15?
The hand is long and thin.
quiz.rationale: A good Driving Question Board entry is a real mathematical question. The other choices are statements of what can be seen, not questions.
quiz.placement: Observe: groups write their most important 'Wonder' question on a sticky note for the Driving Question Board

quiz.prompt: A group pins the base of a 20 cm card arrow to a sheet of paper. They measure a straight line from the pin to the tip of the arrow and get 20 cm. They then turn the arrow clockwise by any amount and measure again. What should they find for the straight-line distance from the pin to the tip?
choices: 0 cm, because the pin does not move
Less than 20 cm, because the arrow has turned away from where it started
More than 20 cm, because the tip has moved further away
About 20 cm, the same as before
quiz.rationale: Careful measurement in the improvised clock kit gives the same distance before and after turning, to within about 2 mm. This is an observation from the investigation; the lesson does not yet ask why it happens.
quiz.placement: Explain: improvised clock kit investigation (measuring tip and halfway-dot distances before and after rotation)

quiz.prompt: In the card-arrow investigation, one learner measures the distance from the pin to the tip by running a string along the curved path that the tip traced while turning. Is this the distance from the centre to the tip?
choices: No, because the curve is only the distance for the halfway dot
Yes, because any path from the pin to the tip gives the same distance
Yes, because the tip travelled along the curve
No, because the distance from the centre is the straight line from the pin to the point, not along the curve
quiz.rationale: The distance from the centre to a point is measured along a straight line from the pin to that point. The curved path is the arc traced by the tip, which is a different measurement.
quiz.placement: Explain: improvised clock kit investigation (teacher checks for confusing distance from the centre with arc length)

quiz.prompt: In the card-arrow investigation, the pin holds the base of the arrow still while the arrow turns. In mathematics, what is the pin called?
choices: The angle of rotation
The image
The clockwise point
The centre of rotation
quiz.rationale: The fixed point that the object turns about is called the centre of rotation. The amount of turning is the angle of rotation.
quiz.placement: Explain: vocabulary introduced after the investigation (centre of rotation, angle of rotation, clockwise, anticlockwise)

quiz.prompt: The tip of a clock's minute hand traces a circular arc about a fixed point. The hand does not stretch, shrink or flip over. Which word best names this kind of motion?
choices: Translation, because the hand slides in a straight line
Enlargement, because the hand gets longer
Reflection, because the hand makes a mirror image
Rotation, because the hand turns about a fixed point
quiz.rationale: Turning about a fixed centre without changing size or shape is a rotation. It is not a slide (translation) or a mirror flip (reflection).
quiz.placement: Model: Rotation Model Journal Page 1, Model Statement on what kind of motion the clock hand performs

quiz.prompt: The minute hand of the clock on the University of Nairobi Administration Block moves from 12:00 to 12:15. Which of these stays the SAME?
choices: The angle the hand makes with the 12 mark
The direction the hand points
The length of the hand and the distance of each point on it from the centre of the clock
The position of the tip of the hand
quiz.rationale: The hand does not stretch or shrink, so its size, its shape and the distance of every point from the centre stay the same. Only its direction changes.
quiz.placement: Predict: retrieval of the clock tower minute hand at 12:00, 12:15, 12:30 and 12:45 and the prediction frame

quiz.prompt: A learner pins a triangle cutout ABC to a sheet of paper at point O and turns it 90° clockwise. What happens to the pin point O?
choices: It does not move, because it is the only fixed point (the centre of rotation)
It moves to the middle of the image
It moves 90° clockwise with the triangle
It moves a short distance, then stops
quiz.rationale: The centre of rotation is invariant. The pin stays in the same place while every other point of the cutout turns about it.
quiz.placement: Part: Set-up and Q2 'Did the pin point O move at any point?'

quiz.prompt: Triangle ABC is rotated 90° clockwise about O. Vertex A is 8 cm from O and vertex B is 4 cm from O. A learner measures angle AOA′ as 90°. What should angle BOB′ be?
choices: 45°, because B is closer to O
It cannot be known without measuring
180°, because B is half the distance
90°, because every point turns through the same angle about O
quiz.rationale: Every point on the object moves through the same angle about the centre, whatever its distance from O. So angle BOB′ is also 90°.
quiz.placement: Pair 1, Round 1 and analysis Q3: compare angle AOA′, BOB′ and COC′

quiz.prompt: A triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. It is rotated 180° about a pin at point O. Which statement about the image is correct?
choices: The image has longer sides, because the triangle moved a long way round
The image has the same sides but different angles
The image has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm, so it is congruent to the object
The image is a mirror copy, so it is not congruent to the object
quiz.rationale: Rotation keeps lengths and angles unchanged, so the object and its image are congruent. The sides stay 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm.
quiz.placement: Gallery share and discussion: Property 1, congruence (analysis Q1)

quiz.prompt: A learner rotates a triangle 90° anticlockwise about O. Which clockwise rotation about O gives exactly the same image?
choices: 270° clockwise
180° clockwise
360° clockwise
90° clockwise
quiz.rationale: A 90° anticlockwise turn is the same as 360° − 90° = 270° clockwise. It is not the same as 90° clockwise, which puts the image in a different position.
quiz.placement: Analysis Q4 and Property 4: comparing Image 1 (90° clockwise) with Image 3 (90° anticlockwise)

quiz.prompt: The millstone at a posho mill in Kericho turns about its axle. Which statement describes the rotation correctly?
choices: The axle moves round in a circle, while the edge of the stone stays still
The stone becomes bigger as it turns
Points near the edge turn through a bigger angle than points near the axle
The axle stays fixed, and every point of the stone turns through the same angle about it
quiz.rationale: The axle is the centre of rotation, so it is invariant. Every point of the millstone turns through the same angle, and the stone keeps its size and shape.
quiz.placement: Gallery share and discussion: connecting the four properties to the posho mill millstone

quiz.prompt: A learner draws the clock's minute hand at 12:00 and at 12:30 and adds arcs to show the movement. The tip of the hand turns through 180°. Through what angle does a point in the middle of the hand turn?
choices: 180°, because every point on the hand turns through the same angle
90°, because it is only halfway along the hand
It turns through no angle, because it is close to the centre
360°, because it goes all the way round
quiz.rationale: From 12:00 to 12:30 the hand turns through 2 × 90° = 180°. Every point on the hand turns through this same angle, not just the tip.
quiz.placement: Model building: revising the Lesson 1 clock sketch with 90° arcs drawn from several points on the minute hand

lessons.title: Rotating Objects on a Plane Surface — Constructing Images with a Geometrical Set

quiz.prompt: A learner is asked to sketch triangle ABC after a 90° anticlockwise rotation about a point O outside the triangle. Her sketch shows the triangle in exactly the same orientation as the original, only shifted to a new place. Which transformation has she drawn?
choices: A translation (slide)
A reflection (mirror flip)
A rotation about O
An enlargement
quiz.rationale: A shape that keeps the same orientation and is only moved to a new position has been slid, which is a translation. A rotation turns the shape about O, so its orientation changes.
quiz.placement: Predict: sketching where triangle ABC ends up after a 90° anticlockwise rotation about point O

quiz.prompt: In the construction method, the compass is opened to the distance OA and an arc is drawn through A before the image A′ is marked. Why must OA′ be equal to OA?
choices: Because rotation preserves the distance of every point from the centre
Because the image must be larger than the object
Because the protractor needs a ray of the same length
Because the compass cannot be changed once it is set
quiz.rationale: Every point turns on a circular path about the fixed centre, so its distance from the centre does not change. The compass arc shows this circle, which is why OA′ = OA.
quiz.placement: Observe: Step 3 of 'The Clock Construction Method' (measure the distance with the compass)

quiz.prompt: You are constructing the image of vertex A of a triangle about centre O through 90° anticlockwise. You have drawn a ray from O through A. Where should the protractor be placed to measure the 90° angle?
choices: Centre of the protractor at O, with its baseline along the ray from O through A
Centre of the protractor at the point where the compass arc meets the paper edge
Centre of the protractor at O, with its baseline along the horizontal edge of the paper
Centre of the protractor at A, with its baseline along side AB
quiz.rationale: The angle of rotation is measured at the centre O from the ray OA to the new ray OA′. So the protractor's baseline must lie along the ray from O through A, not along a horizontal or a side of the shape.
quiz.placement: Observe: Step 4 of 'The Clock Construction Method' (measure the angle with the protractor)

quiz.prompt: Quadrilateral PQRS is rotated 180° clockwise about a point O inside it. Vertex P is 5 cm from O. Which statement about the image P′ is correct?
choices: P′ is 10 cm from O, on the opposite side of O from P
P′ is 5 cm from O, on a line through O at right angles to OP
P′ is 5 cm from O, on the same ray as P
P′ is 5 cm from O, on the opposite side of O from P, in line with P and O
quiz.rationale: Rotation keeps the distance from the centre at 5 cm. A half-turn of 180° sends P to the opposite side of O along the same straight line through P and O.
quiz.placement: Observe: independent practice with quadrilateral PQRS, centre O inside the shape, rotated 180° clockwise

quiz.prompt: A rectangle is rotated 90° about one of its own corners, and that corner is the centre of rotation. What happens to the corner that sits on the centre?
choices: It moves 90° along an arc around the other corners
It stays in the same place and is its own image
It moves to the opposite corner of the image
It moves to the middle of the rectangle
quiz.rationale: The centre of rotation is invariant. A point at distance 0 from the centre does not move, so the corner on the centre is its own image.
quiz.placement: Explain: Example B – rectangle with the centre at one corner of the shape, rotated 90°

quiz.prompt: A learner rotates an equilateral triangle 270° anticlockwise about a centre O outside the triangle. Which single rotation about the same centre O gives exactly the same image?
choices: A rotation of 90° anticlockwise
A rotation of 180° clockwise
A rotation of 90° clockwise
A rotation of 270° clockwise
quiz.rationale: A full turn is 360°, and 360° − 270° = 90°. Turning 270° anticlockwise ends in the same place as turning 90° clockwise.
quiz.placement: Explain: Example A – equilateral triangle, centre outside, rotated 270° anticlockwise

quiz.prompt: On a clock model, the minute hand starts at 12:00. It turns clockwise about the centre of the clock face until it shows 12:45. Through what angle has the hand turned?
quiz.rationale: One hour is a full turn of 360°. 45 minutes is 45/60 of an hour, so the angle is 45/60 × 360 = 270° clockwise.
quiz.placement: Model: constructing the minute hand position at 12:45 (270° clockwise) on the clock model

lessons.title: Rotation on the Cartesian Plane — Discovering and Applying Coordinate Rules

quiz.prompt: Point P(3, −2) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Using the rule (x, y) → (−y, x), what is the image P′?
quiz.rationale: Substitute x = 3 and y = −2 into (−y, x): −y = 2 and x = 3, so P′ = (2, 3). (−2, −3) comes from the clockwise rule, and (−3, 2) is the 180° image.
quiz.placement: Explain: Problem 1 – rotate P(3, −2) through 90° anticlockwise without drawing

quiz.prompt: A triangle has a vertex at A(4, 1). It is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
quiz.rationale: The 90° clockwise rule is (x, y) → (y, −x). With x = 4 and y = 1, A′ = (1, −4). (−1, 4) is the anticlockwise image, (−4, −1) is the 180° image, and (4, −1) is a reflection in the x-axis, not a rotation.
quiz.placement: Observe: pairs record the 90° CW Image column of the pre-drawn table

quiz.prompt: A mark on a football is at Q(2, 5), with the axle of the ball as the origin. The ball turns 90° clockwise, then a further 180°, both about the axle. (The forward motion of the ball is ignored.) Where does the mark end up?
quiz.rationale: Step 1: 90° clockwise (x, y) → (y, −x) gives Q′ = (5, −2). Step 2: 180° (x, y) → (−x, −y) applied to Q′ gives Q″ = (−5, 2).
quiz.placement: Explain: Kasarani application – football mark Q(2, 5) rotated 90° clockwise then 180°

quiz.prompt: Which coordinate rule gives a rotation of 270° anticlockwise about the origin?
quiz.rationale: A 270° anticlockwise turn ends in the same position as a 90° clockwise turn, so the rule is (x, y) → (y, −x). (−y, x) is 90° anticlockwise, and (−x, −y) is 180°.
quiz.placement: Explain: 'Notice that 270° anticlockwise gives the same image as 90° clockwise' discussion

quiz.prompt: Point R(5, 3) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the centre C(2, 1), which is not the origin. What is the image R′?
quiz.rationale: Translate so C is the origin: (5 − 2, 3 − 1) = (3, 2). Apply (x, y) → (−y, x) to get (−2, 3). Translate back: (−2 + 2, 3 + 1) = (0, 4). (−3, 5) comes from applying the rule directly to R, and (−2, 3) comes from forgetting to translate back.
quiz.placement: Explain: translate-apply-translate-back for R(5, 3) about C(2, 1)

quiz.prompt: Point (6, 8) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin using (x, y) → (−y, x). How far is the image from the origin?
choices: 14 units
8 units
10 units
6 units
quiz.rationale: The image is (−8, 6). Its distance from the origin is √((−8)² + 6²) = √100 = 10, the same as the original point's distance √(6² + 8²) = 10, because rotation preserves distance from the centre.
quiz.placement: Model: final insight that (x, y) → (−y, x) preserves √(x² + y²)

quiz.prompt: On a clock face grid with the centre at the origin, the tip of the minute hand is at (0, 5) at 12:00. At 12:15 the hand has turned 90° clockwise about the centre. Which point is the tip now at?
quiz.rationale: Use the 90° clockwise rule (x, y) → (y, −x): (0, 5) → (5, −0) = (5, 0). The tip points to the right, as the minute hand does at 3 on the clock.
quiz.placement: Model: extension task – rotate the minute-hand tip (0, 5) through multiples of 90°

lessons.title: INVESTIGATE: Finding the Centre and Angle of Rotation

quiz.prompt: A rotation maps point P to its image P'. The centre of rotation is O. Which statement about O must be true?
choices: O is the midpoint of the segment PP'
O is the same distance from P as from P'
O lies on the line joining P and P'
The line OP is perpendicular to the segment PP'
quiz.rationale: Rotation turns a point about O without changing its distance from O, so OP = OP'. This is why O lies on the perpendicular bisector of PP'. O is the midpoint of PP' only when the angle is 180°.
quiz.placement: Investigation Steps 1–2: constructing the perpendicular bisector of PP'

quiz.prompt: A group finds the centre of rotation by constructing the perpendicular bisectors of PP' and QQ'. Why do they need TWO bisectors and not just one?
choices: Two bisectors are needed only on the Cartesian plane, never on plain paper
One bisector measures the angle and the second measures the direction
One bisector gives only a line of possible centres, and the second bisector cuts it at one point
One bisector is for the object and the other is for the image
quiz.rationale: Every point on one perpendicular bisector is equidistant from P and P', so one bisector gives a whole line of possible centres. A second bisector crosses it at exactly one point, which is the centre.
quiz.placement: Deepening Question Q1: 'Why two and not just one?'

quiz.prompt: A rotation of exactly 180° maps point A(2, 1) to its image A'(6, 5). What are the coordinates of the centre of rotation?
quiz.rationale: For 180°, the centre is the midpoint of A and A'. Midpoint = ((2+6)/2, (1+5)/2) = (4, 3).
quiz.placement: Deepening Question Q3: the 180° case

quiz.prompt: On a Cartesian plane, a rotation maps A(2, 3) to A'(0, 3). What is the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AA'?
quiz.rationale: AA' is a horizontal segment on y = 3 from x = 2 to x = 0. Its midpoint is (1, 3), so the perpendicular bisector is the vertical line x = 1.
quiz.placement: Investigation Sheet 2, Step 1: perpendicular bisector of AA'

quiz.prompt: On a Cartesian plane, the centre of a rotation is found to be O(1, 2). The point A(2, 3) maps to A'(0, 3). What is the angle and direction of the rotation?
choices: 45° anticlockwise
90° clockwise
90° anticlockwise
quiz.rationale: OA goes up and to the right (1, 1), and OA' goes up and to the left (-1, 1). These are perpendicular, so the angle is 90°. The turn from OA to OA' is anticlockwise.
quiz.placement: Investigation Sheet 2, Step 3: measuring the angle and its direction

quiz.prompt: A learner finds a centre O and an angle by construction and measurement. She rotates vertex P to P' correctly, but vertex R does not land on R'. What is the most sensible conclusion?
choices: The rotation is wrong only for R, because each vertex has its own centre
There was an error in the construction or measurement, so the centre or angle needs to be checked again
Rotations do not always map every vertex onto its image
The image must have been enlarged
quiz.rationale: A rotation uses one centre and one angle for every point, and it keeps shape and size. If one vertex fails to land on its image, the centre or angle found is wrong because of a construction or measuring error.
quiz.placement: Investigation Step 4: VERIFY by rotating the object

quiz.prompt: In a photograph, the tip of a clock's minute hand is at 12:00. Twenty minutes later, at 12:20, it has moved to a new position. Through what angle has the minute hand turned clockwise about the clock's centre?
quiz.rationale: The minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, which is 6° per minute. In 20 minutes it turns 6 × 20 = 120°, which matches the move from 12 to 4 on the clock.
quiz.placement: Clock extension: Nairobi clock at 12:00 and 12:20

lessons.title: Rotational Symmetry of Plane Figures and Solids

quiz.prompt: A group pins a paper equilateral triangle at its centre and turns it clockwise. It covers its outline exactly again at some angles up to one full turn. At which angles does it fit its outline?
quiz.rationale: An equilateral triangle fits its outline every 360° ÷ 3 = 120°, so at 120°, 240° and 360°. This gives order 3.
quiz.placement: Step 1: rotating the equilateral triangle cutout about the pinned centre

quiz.prompt: One group records 'order 6' for a square cutout turned about its centre in one full 360° turn. What is the correct order of rotational symmetry of the square, and why?
choices: Order 2, because a square only fits after 180°
Order 6, because a square has six edges and corners counting both
Order 4, because it fits its outline at 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°
Order 8, because a square has four sides and four corners
quiz.rationale: A square fits its outline every 360° ÷ 4 = 90°, giving four positions in a full turn, so the order is 4. Order 6 comes from miscounting.
quiz.placement: Step 1: repeating the investigation for the square and the regular hexagon, group record check

quiz.prompt: A Kikuyu kiondo basket has a regular hexagon weave pattern when viewed from above. What is the angle between one position where the pattern looks identical and the next, as it is turned about its centre?
quiz.rationale: A regular hexagon has order 6, so the angle between identical positions is 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.
quiz.placement: Step 3: compiling the class table and matching the kiondo basket image to the hexagon row

quiz.prompt: A right circular cone stands on its base. It is turned about the vertical axis through its apex and the centre of its base. What is its order of rotational symmetry about this axis?
choices: Infinite order, because it looks the same after every turn
Order 2, because it has a round base and a point
Order 4, because it has a vertical axis
Order 1, because it only fits after a full turn
quiz.rationale: A cone is perfectly round about its vertical axis, so it looks identical after every amount of turning. Its order is infinite.
quiz.placement: Step 2: handling the solid models (cone prompt about every position around the vertical axis)

quiz.prompt: A triangular prism has ends that are equilateral triangles. An axis joins the centres of the two triangular ends. What is the order of rotational symmetry of the prism about this axis?
choices: Order 3
Order 6
Order 2
Order 1
quiz.rationale: Turning the prism about this axis, the equilateral triangle ends fit onto themselves every 120°, so the order is 3. Order 2 comes from confusing the rectangular faces with the triangle symmetry.
quiz.placement: Step 2: identifying axis and order for the triangular prism

quiz.prompt: A regular pentagon is not cut out. Using angle = 360° ÷ n, what is the smallest angle that turns it onto itself?
quiz.rationale: A regular pentagon has order 5, so the smallest angle is 360° ÷ 5 = 72°.
quiz.placement: Task A: regular pentagon, predict its order using angle = 360°/n

quiz.prompt: Look at just the minute hand of a clock, a single straight arm turned about the centre of the clock. What is its order of rotational symmetry, and why?
choices: Order 4, because it points at 12, 3, 6 and 9
Order 2, because it looks the same after a half turn
Order 1, because it only fits onto itself after a full 360° turn
Order 12, because the clock has 12 numbers
quiz.rationale: The hand only returns to an identical position after 360°, so it maps onto itself once in a full turn. Its order is 1.
quiz.placement: After the class table is complete: the minute hand of the Nairobi clock image

quiz.prompt: The 12 hour-marks of a clock face are equally spaced. Ignoring the numerals, hands and minute marks, through what smallest angle can the clock face be turned so that it maps onto itself?
quiz.rationale: The 12 hour-marks give order 12, so the smallest angle is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°.
quiz.placement: DQB update: capstone entry on the order of the 12 hour-marks of the clock face

quiz.prompt: A learner draws a regular hexagon on a coordinate grid to model a 3-D kiondo basket. Which statement is a limitation of this model?
choices: It shows too many vertices to be a regular hexagon
It only shows a 2-D cross-section, so it does not show the axis and depth of the 3-D basket
It cannot show that the hexagon has order 6
It cannot show a 60° rotation between vertices
quiz.rationale: A flat hexagon shows only one cross-section. The full symmetry of the 3-D basket must also account for its axis and depth.
quiz.placement: Model building: adding the hexagon layer and the model limitation note

lessons.title: Rotation and Congruence: Same Shape, Different Story

quiz.prompt: A scalene triangle is rotated 90° about a point. The object and its image are cut out of paper and kept flat and face up on a desk. What is needed to make the image fit exactly onto the object?
choices: Sliding alone, with no turning
The image can never fit, because rotation changes the size
Sliding and turning on the desk, with no flipping over
Flipping the cutout over so it faces down
quiz.rationale: A rotated image fits its object by sliding and turning while it stays flat and face up. No flipping is needed, so rotation gives direct congruence.
quiz.placement: Part: Observe - three-action test on Pair B (scalene triangle and its rotation image)

quiz.prompt: An irregular quadrilateral and its reflection image are cut out of paper. Sliding and turning the image flat on the desk does not make it fit the object. What must you do to make it fit?
choices: Slide it further across the desk
Turn it through a bigger angle on the desk
Flip the cutout over so it faces down
Make the cutout larger
quiz.rationale: A reflected image is a mirror image, so it fits only after the cutout is flipped over. This is the signature of opposite congruence.
quiz.placement: Part: Observe - three-action test on Pair C (irregular quadrilateral and its reflection image)

quiz.prompt: Triangle ABC has its vertices in the order A→B→C going anticlockwise. The triangle is reflected in a mirror line to give A'B'C'. Which statement is correct about the order A'→B'→C'?
choices: It goes clockwise, so the image is oppositely congruent
It also goes anticlockwise, so the image is directly congruent
It goes clockwise, so the image is directly congruent
It goes anticlockwise, so the image is oppositely congruent
quiz.rationale: A reflection reverses the order of the vertices, so anticlockwise becomes clockwise. This is opposite congruence. Direct congruence keeps the same sense.
quiz.placement: Part: Explain - introducing direct and opposite congruence and completing the three-column table

quiz.prompt: Triangle PQR has vertices P(1, 2), Q(4, 2) and R(4, 6). It is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin to give P'(-2, 1), Q'(-2, 4) and R'(-6, 4). What is the length of P'R'?
choices: 7 units
5 units
3 units
25 units
quiz.rationale: P'R' = sqrt((-6 - (-2))² + (4 - 1)²) = sqrt(16 + 9) = sqrt(25) = 5. This equals PR = 5, so the sides are equal and the triangles are congruent.
quiz.placement: Part: Explain - worked-example card, part (a) verifying congruence by measuring side lengths

quiz.prompt: A learner says: "Rotation turns the shape, so the image must need flipping over to match the object, which makes it opposite congruence." Which reply is correct?
choices: The learner is right, because rotation reverses the order of the vertices
The learner is wrong, because a rotated image is not congruent to its object
The learner is wrong, because rotation keeps the vertex order going the same way round, so no flipping is needed
The learner is right, because any turning is the same as flipping
quiz.rationale: Rotation keeps the order of the vertices going the same way round, for example anticlockwise stays anticlockwise. The image matches the object by sliding and turning flat, so the congruence is direct. Only reflection reverses the order.
quiz.placement: Part: Explain - class discussion 'Rotation turns the shape, so why is the image still directly congruent?'

quiz.prompt: The minute hand of a clock is at 12:00. It then turns to its position at 12:15. What type of congruence connects the two positions of the hand, and why?
choices: Opposite congruence, because the hand has been turned
Opposite congruence, because the hand points in a different direction
They are not congruent, because the hand has moved
Direct congruence, because the hand is turned, not flipped over, so it still fits the first position by turning
quiz.rationale: The hand is only turned about the centre of the clock. Its shape and size do not change and it is not flipped, so the two positions are directly congruent.
quiz.placement: Part: Driving Question Board - clock question 'Minute hand at 12:00 and at 12:15 - direct or opposite congruence?'

quiz.prompt: Which row correctly gives the type of congruence produced by each transformation?
choices: Translation: direct; Rotation: opposite; Reflection: opposite
Translation: direct; Rotation: direct; Reflection: opposite
Translation: opposite; Rotation: direct; Reflection: direct
Translation: direct; Rotation: direct; Reflection: direct
quiz.rationale: Translation and rotation need only sliding and/or turning flat, so they give direct congruence. Reflection needs the cutout flipped over, so it gives opposite congruence.
quiz.placement: Part: Model Building - 'Congruence Landscape' branching diagram

lessons.title: Model Building, Application & Assessment: "Putting It All Together"

quiz.prompt: The minute hand of a clock moves from 12:00 to 12:15. Through what angle, and in which direction, does it turn about the centre of the clock?
choices: 90° clockwise
180° clockwise
90° anticlockwise
15° clockwise
quiz.rationale: The hand makes a full 360° turn in 60 minutes, so in 15 minutes it turns 15/60 × 360 = 90°. Clock hands move clockwise.
quiz.placement: Observe: teacher asks 'What is the angle the minute hand turns through every 15 minutes?'

quiz.prompt: A minute hand turns about the centre of a clock from 12:00 to 12:30. Which statement about the hand is true?
choices: The hand slides sideways to a new position without turning.
The hand flips over like a mirror image and its length changes.
The hand stays the same length and every point on it stays the same distance from the centre.
The hand becomes longer because it has moved further round.
quiz.rationale: Rotation keeps the shape and size of an object, so distances from the fixed centre do not change. Only the direction changes. Flipping is reflection and sliding is translation.
quiz.placement: Observe: 'What stays the same across all four images? What changes?'

quiz.prompt: The tip of a clock's minute hand is at A(0, 5) at 12:00. The centre of the clock is the origin (0, 0). Using the rule (x, y) → (y, −x), where is the tip at 12:15, after a 90° clockwise rotation?
quiz.rationale: Apply (x, y) → (y, −x) to (0, 5): the new point is (5, −0) = (5, 0). This is the 3 o'clock position. (−5, 0) is the anticlockwise answer.
quiz.placement: Part A: rotate A(0,5), B(0,3), C(0,1) to the 12:15 position

quiz.prompt: At 12:00 a point C(0, 1) lies on a clock's minute hand, with the centre at the origin. At 12:45 the hand has turned 270° clockwise, which is the same as 90° anticlockwise, with the rule (x, y) → (−y, x). Where is the image of C?
quiz.rationale: Apply (x, y) → (−y, x) to (0, 1): the new point is (−1, 0). This is the 9 o'clock position. (1, 0) comes from using the clockwise rule by mistake.
quiz.placement: Part A: rotate the hand to the 12:45 position (270° clockwise = 90° anticlockwise)

quiz.prompt: Triangle PQR is rotated to give image P'Q'R'. You want to find the centre of rotation by construction. Which method is correct?
choices: Draw the angle bisector at P. The centre is where it meets the side QR.
Join P to P' and Q to Q'. The centre is where the two lines meet.
Find the midpoint of PP'. That midpoint is the centre.
Draw the perpendicular bisectors of PP' and QQ'. The centre is where they meet.
quiz.rationale: The centre is the same distance from a point and its image, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of each pair PP' and QQ'. The centre is where the bisectors intersect.
quiz.placement: Part B: determine centre and angle of rotation using perpendicular bisectors of PP' and QQ'

quiz.prompt: What is the order of rotational symmetry of the letter 'S' (drawn in its usual shape)?
quiz.rationale: The letter S looks exactly the same after a half-turn (180°) about its centre and again after a full turn, so its order is 2. A quarter-turn (90°) does not fit it back onto itself, so it cannot be order 4.
quiz.placement: Part C: order of rotational symmetry of the regular hexagon, rectangle and letter 'S'

quiz.prompt: A triangular prism has two equilateral triangle ends. It is turned about the axis that joins the centres of the two ends. What is the order of rotational symmetry about this axis?
quiz.rationale: An equilateral triangle fits onto itself every 120°. So the prism fits onto itself 360 ÷ 120 = 3 times in one full turn about this axis.
quiz.placement: Part D: axis and order of rotational symmetry of a triangular prism

quiz.prompt: Triangle ABC is rotated 90° about a point to give triangle A'B'C'. Which statement is correct?
choices: Triangle A'B'C' is a mirror image of triangle ABC.
Only the angles stay equal, while the side lengths change.
The two triangles are congruent: all sides and angles are equal.
Triangle A'B'C' is larger because it has turned.
quiz.rationale: Rotation preserves lengths and angles, so the image is congruent to the object. It is a direct congruence with the same orientation type, not a mirror image like a reflection.
quiz.placement: Part E: congruence from rotation (pairs of triangles on a grid)
